levels.MEASURED: A value from a named measured data product, aggregated to the cell.
levels.DERIVED: A stated formula applied to measured values (e.g. slope from a DEM, amplitude from two temperatures, sun geometry).
levels.MODELLED: A model, an interpolated climatology, an assumed mapping or a value set by definition; not a measurement of the cell.
levels.UNDOCUMENTED: A cached array whose product, date and method are not documented. No variable of this dataset has this level (defined for other tables only).
levels.NO_DATA: The variable has no data on this body (not applicable); its values are empty, never 0.

comparability_statuses.comparable: Same physical quantity and definition on both bodies; used in the similarity.
comparability_statuses.comparable_with_caveat: Used in the similarity; the reason says how the two values differ (show it).
comparability_statuses.not_comparable: Not the same quantity on both bodies (or no data on one): left out of the similarity and the twin search; still counts in suitability.

variables.name: elevation_m
variables.label: Elevation
variables.description: Mean surface height of the cell. Earth: land only, above the EGM2008 geoid (sea level). Moon: above the 1737.4 km reference sphere.

comparability.reason: Earth heights are above the geoid (sea level) and only over land; lunar heights are above an arbitrary 1737.4 km sphere. Not weighted by any mission (only the Earth land gate uses it).

EARTH.product: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model, 60 arc-second surface elevation (ice surface), NOAA NCEI
EARTH.licence_credit: US Government work, no restrictions. Credit: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74

EARTH.caveat: area-weighted mean land elevation above the EGM2008 geoid (sea level); empty for cells with no land pixel. The Moon's elevation_m is relative to a 1737.4 km sphere, so the common gate elevation_m >= 1 has no physical meaning there.

Cell latitudes are the product's WGS84 GEODETIC latitudes (not converted to planetocentric; difference <= 0.19 deg)

variables.name: mask_fraction
variables.label: Land share
variables.description: Earth: share of the cell that is land (ESA CCI land cover; inland water counts as water). Moon: 1 by definition.

comparability.reason: Earth land share against a lunar value that is 1 by definition. Gate only.

EARTH.product: ESA CCI / Copernicus C3S Land Cover map 2020 (LCCS legend), lccs_class, 300 m; tiled COG copy on Microsoft Planetary Computer (collection esa-cci-lc), anonymous access

EARTH.provenance_caveat: land share EXCLUDING inland water (lakes, large rivers count as water); classification product, not a coastline vector; year 2020

MOON.provenance_caveat: Set by definition, not measured. The engine gate mask_fraction >= 0.3 passes everywhere.

variables.name: slope_300m_deg
variables.label: Slope (rover)
variables.description: The rover's slope variable. No global product has a 300 m baseline: it is read from the isotropic km-baseline slope (see true_baseline).

comparability.reason: Same definition on both bodies (central differences, isotropic baseline, cos-lat weighted cell mean) and near-equal baselines (3.7 km on Earth, 3.8 km on the Moon; true_baseline per body). Both are km-baseline slopes, not 300 m slopes.

EARTH.column_override_why: Every slope variable the missions name (rover slope_300m_deg and solar slope_deg, both aliased to slope_deg) is read from the isotropic-baseline column instead, on both bodies. The literal slope_deg uses a one-pixel east-west spacing that shrinks as cos(latitude), so near the poles the east-west baseline falls to tens of metres and inflates the slope; both builders documented this (provenance rows of slope_deg, slope_p90_deg and slope_iso_deg). slope_iso_deg keeps the same baseline in both directions at every latitude (true baseline read from the provenance row). Equal to slope_deg at low latitudes.
EARTH.product: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model, 60 arc-second surface elevation (ice surface), NOAA NCEI
EARTH.licence_credit: US Government work, no restrictions. Credit: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74
EARTH.native_resolution: 60 arc-second (1.853 km N-S; 1.853*cos(lat) km E-W); heights in m above the EGM2008 geoid
EARTH.aggregation: AREA-WEIGHTED (cos lat) mean of the land-pixel slopes
EARTH.formula: as slope_deg, but dz/dx = (z(x+s) - z(x-s)) / (2 s dx) with s = max(1, 1/cos(lat)) pixels (linear interpolation along the row; bracketing pixels must be land): east-west baseline = max(2 dx, 2 dy) = 3.706 km in both directions
EARTH.caveat: no open global DEM-derived product at a 300 m baseline is used here; slopes at a ~3.7 km baseline are systematically LOWER than 300 m slopes, so the mission's 300 m thresholds (0.5-15 deg) are not directly comparable. slope_p90_deg is a stricter alternative. Poleward of ~85 deg use slope_iso_deg (3.706 km baseline in both directions), as for the Moon.
EARTH.provenance_caveat: Companion column added during verification, same definition as the Moon's slope_iso_deg. Use it poleward of ~85 deg, where the literal 1-pixel east-west spacing of slope_deg shrinks to tens of metres and the slope is noisy. Not a 300 m slope.

Equal to slope_deg at low latitudes.

variables.name: rough_300m_m
variables.label: Roughness (rover)
variables.description: The rover's roughness variable. RMS height difference (deviogram) at a lag of about 1.9 km, not 300 m (see true_baseline).

comparability.reason: Same deviogram definition on both bodies at near-equal lags (1.853 km on Earth, 1.895 km on the Moon). Both are km-lag roughness, not 300 m roughness.

EARTH.product: ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model, 60 arc-second surface elevation (ice surface), NOAA NCEI
EARTH.licence_credit: US Government work, no restrictions. Credit: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74
EARTH.native_resolution: 60 arc-second (1.853 km N-S; 1.853*cos(lat) km E-W); heights in m above the EGM2008 geoid
EARTH.aggregation: over all land-land pairs in the cell: south-neighbour pairs (exactly one pixel = 1.853 km apart) and east pairs taken at the SAME metric lag, i.e. 1/cos(lat) pixels along the row (linear interpolation between the two bracketing pixels, both must be land); pooled
EARTH.formula: sqrt(mean((z(x+L) - z(x))^2)), L = 1.853 km in both directions = deviogram (Rosenburg et al. 2011) at a lag of one DEM pixel; identical definition to the Moon table (lag 1.895 km)
EARTH.true_baseline: lag of one DEM pixel = 1.853 km in both directions (east pairs taken 1/cos(lat) pixels apart, linear interpolation), same definition as the Moon (1.895 km)
EARTH.caveat: RMS height difference (deviogram) at a ~1.85 km lag, not 300 m; values grow with lag, so they are larger than a 300 m roughness would be. The mission thresholds (5-650 m) were written for 300 m.
EARTH.provenance_caveat: BASELINE: isotropic lag 1.853 km (one ETOPO pixel N-S); not 300 m, so values are larger than a 300 m roughness. Fixed during verification: the first build used a 1-pixel east lag (1.853*cos(lat) km), which made roughness too low away from the equator (new/old median ratio 1.075 at 30-60 deg, 1.26 at 60-75 deg, 1.44 poleward of 75 deg) and differed from the Moon definition

MOON.aggregation: RMS over all north-south and east-west neighbour pairs whose first pixel is in the cell
MOON.formula: roughness = sqrt(mean((z(x+L) - z(x))^2)), lag L = one DEM pixel = 1.8952 km (deviogram, Rosenburg et al. 2011, JGR 116, E02001). North-south pairs: adjacent rows. variables.name: rock_or_bare_frac
variables.label: Bare or sparsely vegetated fraction
variables.description: Earth: bare plus sparse-vegetation share of the land pixels (ESA CCI land cover). Moon: 1 by definition (no vegetation); not rock abundance.

comparability.reason: Earth bare-or-sparse-vegetation share from a land-cover classification against a lunar value that is 1 by definition; Moon-likeness would only measure how bare an Earth cell is.

EARTH.product: ESA CCI / Copernicus C3S Land Cover map 2020 (LCCS legend), lccs_class, 300 m; tiled COG copy on Microsoft Planetary Computer (collection esa-cci-lc), anonymous access
EARTH.licence_credit: ESA CCI Land Cover / C3S licence: free use with attribution. Credit: 'ESA Climate Change Initiative - Land Cover led by UCLouvain (2017)' and 'Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) Climate Data Store: Land cover classification gridded maps from 1992 to present (v2.1.1)'
EARTH.aggregation: count of 300 m pixels per cell
EARTH.formula: (pixels of classes 200,201,202 bare areas + 150,151,152,153 sparse vegetation <15%) / land pixels (not water, not no-data)
EARTH.caveat: bare (CCI 200-202) + sparse vegetation <15% (CCI 150-153) share of land pixels; a land-cover classification, not rock abundance
EARTH.provenance_caveat: bare-or-sparsely-vegetated fraction from a land-cover CLASSIFICATION, NOT a rock abundance and not a measured bare-ground fraction; sparse vegetation classes allow up to 15 % plant cover; bare_frac (classes 200-202 only) is also provided ESA CCI maps many desert shrublands (e.g. Mojave, Colorado Plateau, Tabernas) as shrubland, so the fraction is low there (Death Valley cell 0.05, Hanksville 0.21) although the ground is largely bare.

MOON.formula: 1 for every cell: the team's variable means exposed (unvegetated) ground; the Moon has none
MOON.caveat: 1 by definition (no vegetation). Measured rock abundance is rock_abundance_frac (60S-60N).
MOON.provenance_caveat: NOT rock abundance. Rock abundance is the separate column rock_abundance_frac.

variables.name: temp_k
variables.label: Mean surface temperature
variables.description: Earth: annual mean clear-sky land surface temperature (mean of the ~10:30 and ~22:30 MODIS overpasses). Moon: diurnal mean Diviner bolometric brightness temperature.

comparability.reason: Both are surface (skin) temperatures averaged over the day, but Earth is the mean of two clear-sky overpasses (~10:30 and ~22:30) and the Moon a full diurnal mean of a brightness temperature; Earth has no Antarctic values.

EARTH.product: OpenLandMap long-term MODIS LST climatology (Hengl 2018), derived from NASA MODIS Terra MOD11A2 v006 8-day 1 km LST, 2000-2017: annual day_m, annual night_m, and 12 monthly daynight_m (day minus night) layers
EARTH.licence_credit: CC BY-SA 4.0. Credit: Hengl, T. (2018) Long-term MODIS LST day-time and night-time temperatures, sd and differences at 1 km based on the 2000-2017 time series, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.1420115; MOD11A2 by Wan, Hook, Hulley, NASA LP DAAC
EARTH.native_resolution: 1/120 deg (about 1 km); stored as K*50 (scale 0.02); coverage 87.37 N to about 62 S (no Antarctica)
EARTH.aggregation: mean over 1 km pixels with both day and night values, land cells only
EARTH.caveat: annual mean clear-sky LAND SURFACE temperature (mean of day and night MODIS climatologies), not air temperature; empty in Antarctica
EARTH.provenance_caveat: LAND SURFACE (skin) TEMPERATURE, NOT AIR TEMPERATURE; clear-sky only (cloudy days missing, which biases warm in cloudy climates); mean of ~10:30 and ~22:30 local-time Terra overpasses, not a true 24 h mean; no Antarctica (empty south of about 62 S) Coverage: 18,736 of 25,497 land cells; empty for all of Antarctica.

MOON.product: Diviner Global Cumulative Products (GCP), column tbol
MOON.licence_credit: NASA PDS data: publicly released, no access restrictions; NASA-produced data are not subject to US copyright (licence string not stated on the product page). Credit: Diviner team, UCLA (Williams et al. 2017, Icarus 283:300-325); LRO-L-DLRE-5-GCP-V1.0, product version 1 (files *_002), PDS Geosciences Node
MOON.aggregation: 0.5 deg x 0.5 deg x 0.25 h local-time bins, all nadir data 2009-07-05..2015-04-01. Per 0.5 deg bin: -9999 and non-positive values dropped; bins with >= 40/96 valid local times and longest gap <= 12 bins (3 h) are filled by circular linear interpolation in local time; then the statistic over the 96 bins; then the cos-lat weighted mean of the (up to 4) 0.5 deg bins in the 1 deg cell (count in temp_n_subcells); statistic = time mean
MOON.formula: temp_k = mean over the 96 local-time bins of the diurnal tbol curve, after circular linear interpolation of empty bins (gaps of at most 12 bins = 3 h); labelled DERIVED, not MEASURED, because of that gap filling
MOON.caveat: Diurnal mean surface bolometric brightness temperature, not air temperature.
MOON.provenance_caveat: Bolometric BRIGHTNESS temperature of the surface (radiometric, ~skin), NOT air temperature and not kinetic temperature. Each local-time bin averages all seasons 2009-2015, so at high latitude the max/min of this averaged curve are smoother than the extremes of a single lunation; a 1 deg cell mixes lit and shadowed terrain near the poles.

Hijmans (2017) WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology 37: 4302-4315
EARTH.aggregation: mean over the cell's 10' land pixels
EARTH.formula: per pixel min over the 12 months of tmin (monthly mean of DAILY MINIMUM AIR temperature, 2 m); i.e. the coldest-month mean daily minimum, deg C
EARTH.caveat: WorldClim 2.1 coldest-month mean daily minimum AIR temperature (1970-2000), interpolated; MODELLED; WorldClim licence is non-commercial, no redistribution without permission
EARTH.provenance_caveat: AIR temperature from station interpolation (1970-2000), not surface temperature and not an absolute minimum (single nights are colder) KNOWN WEAKNESS: over the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets WorldClim has few stations; at Dome C the cell gives -49.3 C while the station's coldest-month mean minimum is near -70 C, so treat polar-plateau values as unreliable.

MOON.licence_credit: NASA PDS data: publicly released, no access restrictions; NASA-produced data are not subject to US copyright (licence string not stated on the product page). Credit: Diviner team, UCLA (Williams et al. 2017, Icarus 283:300-325); LRO-L-DLRE-5-GCP-V1.0, product version 1 (files *_002), PDS Geosciences Node
MOON.aggregation: 0.5 deg x 0.5 deg x 0.25 h local-time bins, all nadir data 2009-07-05..2015-04-01. Per 0.5 deg bin: -9999 and non-positive values dropped; bins with >= 40/96 valid local times and longest gap <= 12 bins (3 h) are filled by circular linear interpolation in local time; then the statistic over the 96 bins; then the cos-lat weighted mean of the (up to 4) 0.5 deg bins in the 1 deg cell (count in temp_n_subcells)
MOON.provenance_caveat: SURFACE minimum (pre-dawn), not air temperature (there is no air). Bolometric BRIGHTNESS temperature of the surface (radiometric, ~skin), NOT air temperature and not kinetic temperature. Each local-time bin averages all seasons 2009-2015, so at high latitude the max/min of this averaged curve are smoother than the extremes of a single lunation; a 1 deg cell mixes lit and shadowed terrain near the poles.

variables.name: irradiance_kwh_m2_day
variables.label: Solar irradiance
variables.description: Daily solar energy on a horizontal surface. Earth: surface value under the atmosphere (WorldClim srad). Moon: geometry with no atmosphere, with the LOLA topographic lit fraction near the poles.

comparability.reason: Daily energy on a horizontal surface on both bodies, but the Earth value is a MODELLED climatology of the solar radiation reaching the ground under the atmosphere and clouds (WorldClim interpolation, not a measurement) while the Moon has no atmosphere, and the lunar value is a 24-hour mean over a 29.5-day lunar day.

EARTH.licence_credit: WorldClim licence (https://www.worldclim.org/data/worldclim21.html, checked 2026-11-14): 'The data are freely available for academic use and other non-commercial use. Redistribution or commercial use is not allowed without prior permission.' NOT CC BY: the first build said CC BY 4.0, which was wrong. Publishing these derived 1-degree columns outside a non-commercial academic context may need WorldClim's permission. Credit: Fick, S.E. and R.J. Hijmans (2017) WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology 37: 4302-4315
EARTH.aggregation: mean over the cell's 10' land pixels
EARTH.formula: per pixel sum_m(srad_m * days_m)/365.25 / 3600; srad in kJ m-2 day-1, 1 kWh = 3600 kJ; days_m with February = 28.25
EARTH.caveat: WorldClim 2.1 srad annual mean (interpolated), global horizontal
EARTH.provenance_caveat: incoming surface solar radiation on a horizontal plane (global horizontal), interpolated climatology 1970-2000, NOT a satellite (CERES) product; CERES could not be obtained without a login

MOON.product: solar constant (NSSDC Moon fact sheet) + exact geometry; LOLA topographic illum_frac where it exists (|lat| >= 65.5)
MOON.licence_credit: NASA NSSDC fact sheet; NASA Photojournal PIA13720
MOON.formula: Horizontal surface, no atmosphere, Sun-Moon distance 1 au, per 24-hour Earth day. Geometric: Q = S0 * <max(0, sin h)> * 24/1000, S0 = 1361.0 W/m2, sin h = sin(lat) sin(d) + cos(lat) cos(d) cos(H), sin d = sin(eps) sin(L), time mean over H and L uniform. Where the LOLA topographic illum_frac exists: Q = S0 * illum_frac * <sin h | h > 0> * 24/1000 (the topographic lit fraction replaces the geometric daylight fraction; multiplying the geometric Q by illum_frac would count the night twice). Results (cell centres): 0.5 deg (equator) 10.40, 45.5 deg 7.29, 85.5 deg 0.840 kWh/m2/day (geometric); 85.5 deg with the median topographic illum_frac of that row 0.247: 0.415 kWh/m2/day (<sin h | h>0> at 85.5 deg = 0.0514)
MOON.caveat: Horizontal surface, per 24 h, DERIVED; uses the LOLA topographic illum_frac (Mazarico 2011 simulation) at |lat| >= 65.5.
MOON.provenance_caveat: Horizontal panel. A vertical sun-tracking panel at the pole receives ~S0 whenever lit (about 32.7 kWh/m2 per 24 h at illum_frac 1); the engine's thresholds were written for horizontal Earth irradiance. Lunar day = 29.53 Earth days, so 'per day' is a long-run mean.

variables.name: sun_elev_max_deg
variables.label: Maximum sun elevation
variables.description: Highest sun elevation over the year at the cell-centre latitude (formula, flat horizon).

comparability.reason: Same formula on both bodies (90 - max(0, |lat| - obliquity), flat horizon), each with its own obliquity.

EARTH.product: Formula (no download); Earth obliquity IAU 2006 mean obliquity at J2000 = 84381.406 arcsec = 23.4392794 deg
EARTH.version: IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36, ch. 5
EARTH.licence_credit: n/a (formula); cite IERS Conventions 2010 (Petit & Luzum eds.)
EARTH.native_resolution: exact, evaluated at each cell-centre latitude
EARTH.provenance_caveat: geometric centre of the Sun, no refraction; obliquity at J2000

MOON.formula: 90 - max(0, |lat| - eps), eps = 1.54 deg (Sun centre, no refraction)
MOON.provenance_caveat: Flat horizon; local topography can raise or block the Sun.

variables.name: sun_low_frac_0_5deg
variables.label: Low-sun fraction
variables.description: Share of daylight time with the sun 0-5 degrees above a flat horizon (formula).

comparability.reason: Same formula on both bodies (share of daylight with the sun 0-5 degrees high, flat horizon), each with its own obliquity.

EARTH.product: Formula (no download); Earth obliquity IAU 2006 mean obliquity at J2000 = 84381.406 arcsec = 23.4392794 deg
EARTH.version: IERS Conventions (2010), IERS Technical Note 36, ch. 5
EARTH.licence_credit: n/a (formula); cite IERS Conventions 2010 (Petit & Luzum eds.)
EARTH.native_resolution: exact, evaluated at each cell-centre latitude
EARTH.formula: time with 0 < h <= 5 deg divided by time with h > 0 over a year; sin(h)=sin(lat)sin(dec)+cos(lat)cos(dec)cos(H); sin(dec)=sin(eps)sin(L); L and H uniform in time (1440 x 2880 samples)
EARTH.caveat: formula; fraction of daylight time with the Sun 0-5 deg high
EARTH.provenance_caveat: circular orbit (eccentricity 0.0167 ignored, which shifts season lengths by about 3 %); Sun treated as a point; no refraction; flat horizon (no terrain shadowing)

MOON.formula: (time with 0 < h < 5 deg) / (time with h > 0), year average; quadrature on 720 seasons x 2880 hour angles; sin h as for irradiance; Sun centre, no refraction
MOON.provenance_caveat: Equals 1 poleward of ~85 deg (the Sun never exceeds 5 deg).

variables.name: thermal_inertia_class
variables.label: Thermal inertia class
variables.description: Earth: ASSUMED mapping from ESA CCI land-cover classes (class_mappings.json). Moon: 'regolito' everywhere by assumption.

comparability.reason: Earth classes are an assumed mapping from land cover; the lunar value is 'regolito' everywhere by assumption. A label match would say nothing physical.

EARTH.product: ESA CCI / Copernicus C3S Land Cover map 2020 (LCCS legend), lccs_class, 300 m; tiled COG copy on Microsoft Planetary Computer (collection esa-cci-lc), anonymous access
EARTH.licence_credit: ESA CCI Land Cover / C3S licence: free use with attribution. Credit: 'ESA Climate Change Initiative - Land Cover led by UCLouvain (2017)' and 'Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) Climate Data Store: Land cover classification gridded maps from 1992 to present (v2.1.1)'
EARTH.aggregation: category with most 300 m pixels in the cell (water included)
EARTH.formula: each CCI class mapped to roca/regolito/arena/suelo/hielo/agua by class_mappings.json, then plurality
EARTH.caveat: ASSUMED mapping from ESA CCI land-cover classes (class_mappings.json); MODELLED, not a measured thermal inertia
EARTH.provenance_caveat: ASSUMPTION: the class-to-category mapping in class_mappings.json is a judgement, not a measured thermal inertia; ocean cells are 'agua'. Relabelled from DERIVED to MODELLED during verification: an assumed class mapping is an assumption, not a formula from measured values

MOON.licence_credit: NASA Science, Moon facts: 'Nearly the entire Moon is covered by ... lunar regolith'
MOON.provenance_caveat: Stated assumption. Rocky exposures (e.g. fresh crater walls, Tycho) exist locally; see rock_abundance_frac. Regolith thermal inertia ~55 J m-2 K-1 s-1/2 (Hayne et al. 2017).

variables.name: permafrost_class
variables.label: Permafrost class
variables.description: Earth: class from the Obu et al. modelled permafrost probability. Moon: the label 'ninguno' (none) on every cell, a MODELLED label set by definition (team lead decision 5), not a measurement.

comparability.reason: Earth classes come from the Obu et al. modelled permafrost probability; the lunar value is the label 'ninguno' on every cell, a MODELLED label set by definition (team lead decision 5), not a measurement. A label match would say nothing physical.

EARTH.product: Obu et al. permafrost probability (PERPROB) maps, ESA DUE GlobPermafrost: Northern Hemisphere 2000-2016 (PANGAEA 888600) and Antarctic 2000-2017 (PANGAEA 902576)
EARTH.licence_credit: NH: CC BY 3.0; ANT: CC BY 4.0. Credit: Obu, J., Westermann, S., Kaab, A., Bartsch, A. (2018) Ground Temperature Map, 2000-2016, Northern Hemisphere Permafrost, PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.888600; Obu et al. (2019) Ground Temperature Map, 2000-2017, Antarctic, PANGAEA, doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.902576
EARTH.native_resolution: 926.6 m polar stereographic grid (EPSG:3995 NH, EPSG:3031 ANT), nominal 1 km
EARTH.formula: continuo >= 0.90; discontinuo 0.50-0.90; esporadico 0.01-0.50 (sporadic + isolated merged); ninguno < 0.01; see class_mappings.json
EARTH.caveat: from Obu et al. modelled permafrost probability (MODELLED); empty (no data) south of about 18-25 N except Antarctic outcrops, on ice sheets, and on cells without CCI land
EARTH.provenance_caveat: EMPTY (no data) where the maps have no pixel: the NH map stops at about 18-25 N (Mauna Kea at 19.5 N is mapped and is 'ninguno' at 1 km), so Andean, East African and other low-latitude mountain permafrost is missing, not 'ninguno'; also glaciers and ice sheets (Greenland, Antarctic ice sheet). Also empty on cells with no CCI land (18 coastal/ocean cells had a class before verification)

MOON.formula: 'ninguno' in every cell (label set by definition)
MOON.caveat: 'ninguno' on every cell: a MODELLED label set by definition (no terrestrial-type permafrost on the Moon), not a measurement.
MOON.provenance_caveat: MODELLED label, not a measurement: terrestrial permafrost (ground frozen for two or more years, with seasonal thaw of liquid water) does not exist on the Moon, so every cell is labelled 'ninguno' (none). It says nothing about lunar cold traps or buried ice; the cold-trap analogue is tmin_k / tmax_k < 110 K, not estimated here.
